textual.context: The speaker presents the material as instructional preparation for a registration process; the source does not state that a transaction was completed or that any outcome was received.
textual.potential_relevance: Wallet funding, gas-fee allocation, referral-link entry and process acceptance are presented as connected steps for obtaining registration slots; later review would need to assess what the slots provide and the nature of the requested crypto commitment.
textual.limitations: These records do not establish the recipient of funds, whether any transfer occurred, what '630 boost' means, what the slots provide, or where the referral link leads.

visual.observation: A Forsage page for Tron displays an entrance fee of 200 TRX, claims that participants' earnings exceed $80 million, and provides a "Register TRX" button.
visual.context: Promotional registration page; the page also lists benefits and a possible transaction-error disadvantage.
visual.potential_relevance: A stated crypto payment requirement and registration action are directly linked to a claimed participant-earnings outcome.
visual.limitations: These frames do not establish whether the earnings claim is accurate, whether any payment occurred, or what users receive after registering.

visual.observation: A Forsage landing page shows a countdown timer, participant/joined-in-24-hours figures, and "Login to your account" and "Register" controls.
visual.context: Promotional onboarding page with visible registration controls.
visual.potential_relevance: Urgency and participation-count framing are presented directly alongside account-access and registration actions.
visual.limitations: The sampled frames cannot establish whether the countdown reflects a real deadline, whether registration was completed, or whether any benefit depends on acting before it ends.

visual.observation: An automatic-registration screen asks the user to check the ID of an inviter, shows an inviter ID field containing 3590, and offers automatic registration with instructions for smartphone, PC, or manual registration.
visual.context: Referral-style onboarding interface; the requiredness of the inviter field and any benefit to the inviter are not shown.
visual.potential_relevance: An explicit inviter-identifier step is connected to the same registration flow that includes paid TRX registration and an earnings claim.
visual.limitations: These frames do not show whether the inviter receives compensation, whether registration requires payment in this step, or whether the account was created.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is scam content because it actively instructs viewers to fund and register for Forsage BUSD slots using a referral link, rather than merely discussing the service. The associated Forsage screens present tiered entry options, participant earnings claims and an invite-ID automatic registration flow, while the description promotes a successful team and urges group members to start working. Together, these observations show recruitment-dependent participation and earnings claims central to the video's call to action.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: S06 fits because participation is organized around referral links, slots, invite IDs and a team structure, with earnings attributed to participants across the displayed tiers. The video gives operational registration instructions for joining that structure and tells viewers to prepare the required balance and gas fees.
